speaker: Commander Nothard
line: I didn't expect a froglok. You came out of Guk with the rebels? Shut the door. That's your business until you draw my pay.

speaker: Spiritmaster Zole
line: Guk can still be home, if you wish. A binding only settles where you'll wake.

speaker: Captain Norgam
line: Try the grip. Make a fist for me. There, see? The guard clears the web of your thumb now.

speaker: Captain Norgam
line: A carter told me he had six folk out of Guk under his canvas when he was robbed. Lucky for them the thieves wanted his purse.

speaker: Guard Sareken
line: I remember you at this gate with everything you owned in a bundle. You've filled out that bracer since.

speaker: Delwin Stitchfinger
line: Who darned that cuff for you? Reed thread, unless I'm much mistaken. I've seen work like that on the Guk folk at the docks.

speaker: Captain Norgam
line: I put 'froglok from Guk' on your first pay chit. I put your name on this one, %p. See that I spelled it right.

speaker: Dilina McNerian
line: One of the rebels out of Guk, are you? Set your bundle under my bench. Nobody roots about under there twice.

speaker: Gilderman Vanks
line: Ever ground beetle shell with two river stones? Then you've used a pestle, whatever Dilina chooses to call it.

speaker: Gilderman Vanks
line: When the wagons came through with the folk from Guk, one driver gave up his own seat to an old fellow. I remember a thing like that.

speaker: Dilina McNerian
line: See how the stuff clings to the glass? You had the sense to keep your fingers clear. I usually have to teach that twice.

speaker: Johnny Jorn
line: If they ask where you're from, you can tell them you're one of Dilina's. It'll be the plain truth.

speaker: Dilina McNerian
line: You stoppered it for a long journey. Look, not a drop on your pack. My apprentices usually smell of it for a week.

speaker: Dilina McNerian
line: If you ever put those Guk remedies you know down on paper, I'd like a copy. You can put my book on the shelf beside yours.

speaker: William Corufost
line: A froglok! Come in with the rebels from Guk, did you? Pull up a stool. You'll hear better away from the door.

speaker: Coachman Ronks
line: Just give me the name you sing under. Last party up from Guk thought I wanted the whole family tree.

speaker: Solenia Freyar
line: You'll feel the beat of the blade through the hilt. There, you've got it already.

speaker: Solenia Freyar
line: The folk down by the water were afraid to fill a cup. Some came all the way from Guk to be frightened of a well.

speaker: Guard Sareken
line: One of your people sang for my watch last night. Only three notes in the refrain, and I've had them in my head all day.

speaker: Solenia Freyar
line: That old song you hum has the right of it. Listen to who falls quiet when the last verse comes round.

speaker: Solenia Freyar
line: As for the songs you brought out of Guk, sing them in this hall whenever you please. I'll make room on the bill.

speaker: Denouncer Alshea
line: Some of the rebels who fled Guk have been through these doors. I've dressed their feet. This is the first time one's asked to learn.

speaker: Spiritmaster Keika
line: You may have kin who still say your name over the water in Guk. This binding will do them no harm.

speaker: Sister Falhelm
line: Three families from Guk pitched their blankets by that road. They've little enough to lose.

speaker: Sister Falhelm
line: I saw you steady the jar when I reached for it. Somebody tended sick folk beside you before you came here.

speaker: Guard Sareken
line: Those who came out of Guk still ask me about that road. For once I've some good news for them.

speaker: Sister Falhelm
line: You've seen frightened people take anything they're handed if somebody calls it medicine. Remember the smell of those roots.

speaker: Sister Falhelm
line: If another of your folk comes in with their feet raw from the road, there's a second stool by yours now.

speaker: Malsis
line: A froglok. The last rebel from Guk who climbed those stairs asked for passage money. You're looking at the rings instead.

speaker: Kellina
line: You kept your hands steady when I raised my voice. I suppose it takes more than an irritable tutor to rattle someone out of Guk.

speaker: Kellina
line: I had the cuffs drawn up a little. Catch one on a brazier and we'll both be sorry, dear.

speaker: Kellina
line: You knew to keep it below the lip of the jar. Did someone teach you that back in the marsh?

speaker: Guard Sareken
line: A lad from Guk used to fish that bank before the trouble. First catch I've seen from there in days.

speaker: Fritz Belgor
line: One of your folk taught me to wrap these in rush leaves for the wet crossing. Look, still dry inside.

speaker: Kellina
line: When you came in from Guk you kept your pack on, ready to leave. Look at it now, gathering dust under your own bench.

speaker: Necorik the Ghost
line: A froglok off the Guk boats. Easy to spot, you think? I heard the stair creak before I ever saw your face.

speaker: Athera
line: Necorik says you came all the way out of Guk with the rebels. That much practice walking quietly ought to count for something.

speaker: Athera
line: A family out of Guk can lose everything it owns in one stolen cart. The Coffer counts the cart. I remember what rode in it.

speaker: Athera
line: Nice bit of balance. Those wet planks they lay across the marsh must make our rooftops feel wide.

speaker: Guard Sareken
line: If you're wondering about that bundle the Guk folk left at the gate, nobody's touched it. Even I know a child's shoes when I see them.

speaker: Fritz Belgor
line: You're checking the wrapping! Fair enough. The road from Guk would teach anybody what damp does to a parcel.

speaker: Athera
line: If anyone comes to my door buying the names of the Guk rebels, I've forgotten how to spell every last one.

speaker: Azlynn
line: I heard a porter call you one of the Guk rebels. Tell me, did he decide what you wanted before you got a word out?

speaker: Opanheim
line: Interesting. Even with half the room staring at the froglok, you kept your eyes on my hands.

speaker: Opanheim
line: You can keep the coat you wore out of Guk. I still have the one I came here in, somewhere.

speaker: Azlynn
line: I've watched you check a latch twice and never rattle it once. A useful habit to bring out of Guk.

speaker: Merchant Landi
line: That little rush wick in your pocket would do nicely in a bowl. For the road I'd still want a lantern with glass.

speaker: Tailor Weynia
line: Bend your knee for me. Ah, so that's where the old pair binds. I've only ever cut these for folk who stand straight up.

speaker: Azlynn
line: That porter asked for you yesterday. Took him a while to remember your name, but this time he did.

speaker: Corious Slaerin
line: Gilgash has sold candles to half the rebels out of Guk. You're the first froglok who's climbed my stairs to ask what a candle calls.

speaker: Spiritmaster Keika
line: Did you have time to lay all your people to rest before you left? Forgive me. Bindings put such things in my mind.

speaker: Rathei Slaerin
line: That cord you brought from Guk can stay inside the sleeve. Nobody will see it there.

speaker: Corious Slaerin
line: More than one boat out of that village has carried a passenger from Guk under its nets. Temby remembers who paid passage.

speaker: Merchant Landi
line: Funny. Everyone else holds the bottle up to the light. You checked the cork first. Lost a flask on the road once, eh?

speaker: Agent Wilkenson
line: Keep the names of the folk who came out of Guk with you. I've bought exactly one name today.

speaker: Corious Slaerin
line: I have a place in the House book for your name. I'll leave room for the way you wrote it in Guk.

speaker: Malethai Crimsonhand
line: A froglok out of Guk wants to carry my shield. Good. A rebel has had cause to weigh an oath before swearing it.

speaker: Stolfson Krieger
line: I hear you held your ground in Guk. Let's see what your feet do on dry sand.

speaker: Stolfson Krieger
line: I've seen folk out of Guk walk a whole day beside a wagon so their little ones could ride. Word gets around about a safe road.

speaker: Malethai Crimsonhand
line: Go on, put your arm through. There's a second hole in the strap. The first one sat wrong on your elbow.

speaker: Merchant Landi
line: Hold it to the light if you like. That old trick the reedcutters use works just as well on city oil.

speaker: Tailor Weynia
line: Take a step. Good. I left you enough room to crouch the way you do without splitting my best seam.

speaker: Malethai Crimsonhand
line: You came here with the last of the road dust from Guk still on that shield arm. Look what you're carrying on it now.

speaker: Sivrendesh
line: A froglok this far up the tower! I'd heard the rebels from Guk had found beds by the docks. I hadn't heard we had a scholar.

speaker: Nefar
line: You've kept the little knots in that pack pulled tight. I suppose things were harder to replace on the road out of Guk.

speaker: Nefar
line: That shade ought to hold even in marsh water. If it runs, I'll want a word with the dyer.

speaker: Sivrendesh
line: You know what a loose word can cost the folk who stayed in Guk. I need that sort of discretion here.

speaker: Merchant Landi
line: Careful with the neck. Someone sealed a bottle with marsh wax for me once. Never lost a spoonful, but I nearly broke a tooth.

speaker: Tailor Weynia
line: I remember the first froglok who came off a boat asking for dry cloth. Now I've got your measure chalked on the wall.

speaker: Sivrendesh
line: You may sign the Academy register in the script you used in Guk. Leave room beneath it. Someone else may come up those stairs.

speaker: Master T`an Chen
line: Were you one of the frogloks who rose up in Guk? Come sit with your back to the wall, if that helps you rest.

speaker: Spiritmaster Lo
line: Some still in Guk may speak your name every evening. You'll remember them just as well wherever you wake.

speaker: Mu Nan
line: You waited until I finished speaking. Many who have spent so long listening for pursuit find a quiet room the hardest place to listen.

speaker: Dushaun Anju
line: You turned at the sound of the wind in these tent ropes. I hadn't noticed how much they sound like reeds.

speaker: Duke Geoff Melnorn
line: If you're with the monastery, its word is good in my hall. The guard needn't have kept you on the step.

speaker: Jeeves the Scribe
line: After the last party from Guk passed through, I learned to ask how a traveler spells their name before I set pen to paper.

speaker: Mu Nan
line: You heard the word 'uprising' and still took the time to hear each person speak. That takes practice, especially after Guk.

speaker: Necorik the Ghost
line: One of the scouts who came out with the rebels from Guk? You found my door without asking at the gate. I rather like that.

speaker: Athera
line: Clean work on the scales. I can see where a ranger from the marsh learned to use the edge of a knife.

speaker: Denouncer Alshea
line: A froglok paladin. You must have weighed your oath carefully before you stood with the rebels in Guk.

speaker: Sister Falhelm
line: If a frightened traveler out of Guk sees you wearing that shield, give them a moment to recognize who's behind it.

speaker: Denouncer Alshea
line: The rebels from Guk brought what they could carry. Another druid came through with a handful of wet earth, roots and all. I remember that.

speaker: Sister Falhelm
line: I saw you looking for reeds along the ditch. Even this dry country has things you'll know from home.

speaker: Denouncer Alshea
line: A shaman from the rebels in Guk? One of your people sat up a whole night with a feverish child in this hall. There, by the brazier.

speaker: Sister Falhelm
line: Keep whatever small thing you brought out of Guk close. Sometimes a sickbed calls for a familiar voice before anything else.
